analysis.title: A less hawkish Fed steepens the curve
key_insights: The October FOMC held the policy rate at 3.75-4.00%. Governor Lisa Cook and Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack dissented, both preferring a 25bp hike. The market had expected three dissents.

Rates rose across the curve after the statement, then investors read Chair Kevin Warsh's comments as dovish: quashing inflation is not tied to a fixed calendar date, and he was positive about inflation expectations signposts.
The 2Y Treasury yield fell about 8bp from its intraday peak to 4.70%, and the 2-10Y curve steepened 6bp on the day. With front-end rates lower, the intermediate sector cheapened.
Warsh highlighted tighter financial conditions but did not call them tight. This matches mixed signals in spreads: IG and HY spreads have widened while MBS spreads have tightened.
The market prices a 21bp Fed hike premium for December and 46bp through next March, roughly in line with the house view of two 25bp hikes by March.

The base case is that Democrats regain the House in the mid-term elections next week, producing legislative gridlock whichever party takes the Senate. A divided government would lower the chance of major spending programs and tax cuts, easing upward pressure on term premium and long-end yields.
Front-end rates stay driven by monetary policy. With elevated energy prices and expected Fed hikes, 2Y yields should stay elevated.

Election outcomes mainly affect lawmaking, not macro trends. Government funding talks stay contentious with shutdown risk, and widening federal deficits require higher Treasury issuance regardless of the result.
The Treasury is expected to keep coupon auction sizes unchanged at the 4 November refunding, with USD125bn of nominal supply across 3Y, 10Y and 30Y. TIPS auctions should also be unchanged.
Treasury has shifted borrowing adjustment to bills, which have grown substantially since early October and are now 22% of outstanding marketable debt. This is expected to continue near term.

Refunding focus areas: maturity composition of borrowing, TGA guidance (about USD1trn versus a USD850bn year-end target), and long-end buybacks. Debt Management can cut 20Y or 30Y supply to control long-end rates, but timing is uncertain.

tension_points.bull_case: A Democratic House produces legislative gridlock. That reduces the chance of major spending programs and tax cuts, easing upward pressure on term premium and supporting long-end yields.
tension_points.bear_case: Widening federal deficits require higher Treasury issuance whatever the election result, and shutdown risk persists. Front-end rates stay elevated on Fed hikes and energy prices.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Democrats failing to regain House control in the mid-term elections, which is the base case.
